title: Celebration and Mourning: Inside an Iran at War

sentences.zh: 我凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的球队。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，获取nytimes.com/subscribe上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: On Sunday, the United States and Israel pounded Iran with missiles for a second straight day, destroying more and more power centers of the regime.
sentences.zh: 周日，美国和以色列连续第二天用导弹猛烈轰炸伊朗，摧毁了该政权越来越多的权力中心。

sentences.en: And according to rights groups, bringing the civilian death toll there to well over 100.
sentences.zh: 据人权组织称，那里的平民死亡人数已远超100人。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Iran unleashed a wave of retaliatory attacks that proved deadly.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，伊朗发动了一波致命的报复性袭击。

sentences.en: Three U.S.
sentences.zh: 三名美国

sentences.en: troops were killed in action, becoming the first Americans to die in the war.
sentences.zh: 士兵在行动中阵亡，成为这场战争中首批牺牲的美国人。

sentences.en: As one nation, we grieve for the true American patriots who have made the ultimate sacrifice for our nation.
sentences.zh: 作为一个国家，我们为那些为国做出终极牺牲的真正美国爱国者感到悲痛。

sentences.en: But increasingly, all eyes were on the Iranian government and the millions of citizens who have long opposed it.
sentences.zh: 但人们的目光越来越多地投向了伊朗政府，以及长期反对它的数百万公民。

sentences.en: And the looming question became whether a weakened Islamic republic could actually be toppled by its own people.
sentences.zh: 而随之而来的问题是，一个虚弱的伊斯兰共和国是否真的会被自己的人民推翻。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Farnas Fasehi, brings us the view of this pivotal moment from inside Iran.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事法纳斯·法塞希将从伊朗内部为我们带来这一关键时刻的视角。

sentences.en: Monday, March 2nd.
sentences.zh: 3月2日，星期一。

sentences.en: Farnas, thank you for making time for us on a Sunday.
sentences.zh: 法纳斯，谢谢你在周日抽出时间接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: Really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，迈克尔。

sentences.en: So, Farnas, for the people of Iran and for the massive diaspora of Iranians who live outside of the country,
sentences.zh: 那么，法纳斯，对于伊朗人民以及居住在国外的庞大伊朗侨民来说，

sentences.en: including you, Sunday, today, as we speak, it's one of those hinge days in history.
sentences.zh: 包括你在内，周日，也就是今天，在我们交谈之时，这是历史上关键的一天。

sentences.en: There was a before and there was an after.
sentences.zh: 历史从此有了前与后之分。

sentences.en: And right now, the after is a world in which Iran's supreme leader, who has been in power for over three decades, has been killed and is no longer in power.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这个“后”是一个伊朗最高领袖——他已掌权三十多年——被杀且不再掌权的世界。

sentences.en: It's one of those historic days that I think if for every Iranian, whether you're a supporter of the government or you're an opponent,
sentences.zh: 我认为对于每一位伊朗人来说，无论你是政府的支持者还是反对者，这都是历史性的一天，

sentences.en: whether you live inside or you live outside, this is a new day.
sentences.zh: 无论你住在国内还是国外，这都是崭新的一天。

sentences.en: This is a new Iran.
sentences.zh: 这是一个崭新的伊朗。

sentences.en: From the moment we started hearing about Mr. Khamenei being potentially killed, my phone started buzzing.
sentences.zh: 从我们开始听到哈梅内伊先生可能被杀的消息那一刻起，我的手机就开始响个不停。

sentences.en: I was getting text messages and phone calls from my friends and family members.
sentences.zh: 我收到了朋友和家人的短信和电话。

sentences.en: And I was also getting text messages and calls from some of my sources in Iran who were asking me, do you know anything?
sentences.zh: 我也收到了我在伊朗的一些消息来源发来的短信和电话，他们问我：你知道什么吗？

sentences.en: Is the news true?
sentences.zh: 新闻是真的吗？

sentences.en: Is he gone?
sentences.zh: 他真的不在了吗？

sentences.en: What have you heard?
sentences.zh: 你听到了什么？

sentences.en: No matter what side of the divide you were on, this was a monumental moment.
sentences.zh: 无论你站在哪一边，这都是一个具有里程碑意义的时刻。

sentences.en: And today, Iranians woke up to the first day of history without Mr. Khamenei in power.
sentences.zh: 今天，伊朗人迎来了没有哈梅内伊先生掌权的第一天。

sentences.en: And we don't know exactly what that's going to mean yet.
sentences.zh: 我们还不确定这意味着什么。

sentences.en: But this figure who has loomed very large for almost four decades over the fate of Iranians is gone.
sentences.zh: 但这位近四十年来一直笼罩在伊朗人命运之上的大人物已经不在了。

sentences.en: Some Iranians were celebrating.
sentences.zh: 一些伊朗人在庆祝。

sentences.en: People were pouring to the streets.
sentences.zh: 人们涌向街头。

sentences.en: I had several video calls with several people I know in Tehran who turned on the camera and showed me cars honking on the streets.
sentences.zh: 我和德黑兰的几位熟人进行了视频通话，他们打开摄像头，让我看街上鸣笛的汽车。

sentences.en: People cheering.
sentences.zh: 人们在欢呼。

sentences.en: There were fireworks.
sentences.zh: 有人在放烟花。

sentences.en: People sticking their heads out of the windows and chanting freedom, freedom.
sentences.zh: 人们探出窗外，高呼“自由，自由”。

sentences.en: And this visceral scream, like a scream of relief almoSt.
sentences.zh: 还有那种发自肺腑的尖叫，几乎是一种解脱的尖叫。

sentences.en: And for the diaspora, it was scattered all over the world.
sentences.zh: 对于散布在世界各地的侨民来说，

sentences.en: It was a similar feeling.
sentences.zh: 感觉也是一样的。

sentences.en: I watched a group of family members congregate on FaceTime.
sentences.zh: 我看到一群家人在FaceTime上聚在一起。

sentences.en: Some were in the U.S., some were in Europe, some were in Iran.
sentences.zh: 有的在美国，有的在欧洲，有的在伊朗。

sentences.en: And everybody did a video call and some of them were crying.
sentences.zh: 每个人都参与了视频通话，有些人哭了。

sentences.en: They were just these tears of relief and shock and joy even.
sentences.zh: 那是如释重负、震惊甚至喜悦的泪水。

sentences.en: And then they celebrated with shots.
sentences.zh: 然后他们用酒来庆祝。

sentences.en: And there was a lot of cheers.
sentences.zh: 现场有很多欢呼声。

sentences.en: And when you say diaspora,
sentences.zh: 当你提到侨民时，

sentences.en: you quite literally mean families who were once together in Iran and presumably scattered to the winds across the world once the Islamic revolution came in 1979?
sentences.zh: 你是指那些曾经在伊朗生活在一起，但在1979年伊斯兰革命后被迫散落到世界各地的家庭吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: It feels like a dream for many Iranians that once they used to all live a few blocks from each other and have multi-generational family gatherings.
sentences.zh: 对于许多伊朗人来说，这感觉像是一场梦，他们曾经住在离彼此几个街区的地方，举行多代同堂的家庭聚会。

sentences.en: And under Mr. Khamenei, many of them have not been able to return to Iran.
sentences.zh: 而在哈梅内伊先生统治下，他们中的许多人无法回到伊朗。

sentences.en: And many families have just scattered like stardust all over the world and separated from each other.
sentences.zh: 许多家庭就像星尘一样散落在世界各地，彼此分离。

sentences.en: So that's clearly the segment of Iranians, both inside and outside the country, who may be on the celebratory side of the spectrum in the 24-48 hours since he was killed.
sentences.zh: 所以，这显然是伊朗人中，无论国内还是国外，在哈梅内伊被杀后的24到48小时内，处于庆祝光谱那一端的人群。

sentences.en: What about those who support him?
sentences.zh: 那些支持他的人呢？

sentences.en: Presumably you've been talking to them as well.
sentences.zh: 想必你也和他们谈过。

sentences.en: What would you characterize as their reaction?
sentences.zh: 你会如何描述他们的反应？

sentences.en: For Mr. Khamenei's supporters, this feels like a big loss.
sentences.zh: 对于哈梅内伊先生的支持者来说，这感觉是一个巨大的损失。

sentences.en: His supporters started to come out into the streets.
sentences.zh: 他的支持者开始走上街头。

sentences.en: In large numbers, I'm going to mosques and praying and crying.
sentences.zh: 他们成群结队地去清真寺祈祷和哭泣。

sentences.en: It feels like the ground is shifting under them.
sentences.zh: 感觉脚下的土地正在动摇。

sentences.en: Not only have they lost a religious figure that they revered and believed in, but they've also lost a political leader of a system that they have ideological loyalty to.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅失去了一位他们敬仰和信仰的宗教人物，还失去了一个他们拥有意识形态忠诚的体制的政治领袖。

sentences.en: It feels like that is in jeopardy, that they don't know whether this Islamic Republic that they believe in and they support is going to survive or not without him.
sentences.zh: 感觉这一切都岌岌可危，他们不知道他们所信仰和支持的这个伊斯兰共和国在他死后是否还能生存下去。

sentences.en: And you know, this is the reality of Iran, Michael.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是伊朗的现实，迈克尔。

sentences.en: This polarized society.
sentences.zh: 这个两极分化的社会。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And one wonders, whatever comes next, whatever form of government comes next, how are you going to bring these two sides anywhere close to each other, or is that even possible?
sentences.zh: 人们不禁会想，无论接下来会发生什么，无论未来是什么形式的政府，你该如何让这两派人靠近，或者这根本可能吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because the people doing shots in their homes, uncorking champagne,
sentences.zh: 因为那些在家里喝酒、开香槟庆祝的人，

sentences.en: those people would seem to have a very hard time reconciling their reactions and their whole worldview with those who are clinging to photos of the now late Supreme Leader in the streets.
sentences.zh: 似乎很难将他们的反应和整个世界观与那些在街上紧抱着已故最高领袖照片的人调和起来。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I don't know how these two sides are going to reconcile.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这两派人该如何和解。

sentences.en: If you had to estimate, Farnas, how big would you describe both of those camps as?
sentences.zh: 法纳斯，如果你必须估算一下，你会如何描述这两个阵营的规模？

sentences.en: The supporters, the mourners versus the dissidents, the opponents, those celebrating his death.
sentences.zh: 支持者、哀悼者与异见者、反对者、那些庆祝他死亡的人。

sentences.en: I would say that the overwhelming majority of the population in Iran are opponents of the regime, about 80 percent, and the core supporters are about 20 percent.
sentences.zh: 我认为伊朗绝大多数人口是政权的反对者，约占80%，而核心支持者约占20%。

sentences.en: And I think we can sort of draw this conclusion from voting patterns.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以从投票模式中得出这个结论。

sentences.en: In the past couple of years, when there's been presidential elections or parliamentary elections, Iranians, who are hardcore believers of the regime,
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，每当有总统选举或议会选举时，那些政权的铁杆信徒，

sentences.en: have gone to polls around 20 percent.
sentences.zh: 投票率都在20%左右。

sentences.en: It's been 20 percent of the population.
sentences.zh: 也就是占人口的20%。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So you're extrapolating from that, which seems quite reasonable.
sentences.zh: 所以你是从这个数据推断出来的，这看起来很合理。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We can, I think, draw from that.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以从中得出结论。

sentences.en: And also, like, in January, literally every small and big town all over Iran saw protests against the government, including the religious sort of strongholds of the government,
sentences.zh: 而且，就像一月份那样，伊朗各地大大小小的城镇都出现了反政府抗议活动，包括政府的宗教堡垒，

sentences.en: where there were lots of people out calling for the end of this Islamic regime.
sentences.zh: 那里有很多人走上街头，呼吁结束这个伊斯兰政权。

sentences.en: If we look at the demographics of the protesters who were killed in January, they're from all ethnic groups, from a large geographic area in Iran,
sentences.zh: 如果我们看看一月份被杀的抗议者的背景，他们来自所有民族，来自伊朗广阔的地理区域，

sentences.en: and different socioeconomic backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 以及不同的社会经济背景。

sentences.en: Well, because his death is so fresh and the reactions as you are describing them are so different, let's talk about this man who is inspiring such profound reactions, Khamenei.
sentences.zh: 好吧，因为他的死讯还很新鲜，而且正如你所描述的那样，各方的反应截然不同，让我们谈谈这位引发如此强烈反应的人——哈梅内伊。

sentences.en: And why he inspires such strong reactions.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么他会引发如此强烈的反应。

sentences.en: Mr. Khamenei is the second supreme leader of Iran.
sentences.zh: 哈梅内伊先生是伊朗的第二任最高领袖。

sentences.en: The first was founding supreme leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.
sentences.zh: 第一任是开国最高领袖阿亚图拉鲁霍拉·霍梅尼。
zh_words: 阿亚图拉鲁霍拉·霍梅尼

sentences.en: He came to power in 1979 after the Islamic revolution that toppled the monarchy.
sentences.zh: 他在1979年推翻君主制的伊斯兰革命后上台。

sentences.en: Twelve days ago, the Ayatollah was operated on in an attempt to stem intestinal bleeding.
sentences.zh: 十二天前，阿亚图拉接受了手术，试图阻止肠道出血。

sentences.en: Early yesterday, he suffered a heart attack.
sentences.zh: 昨天早些时候，他心脏病发作。

sentences.en: He whispered Muslim prayers and died.
sentences.zh: 他低声念着穆斯林祈祷词，随后去世。

sentences.en: Iran has named a successor to the Ayatollah Khomeini, less than a day after the Ayatollah's death in a Tehran hospital.
sentences.zh: 在阿亚图拉·霍梅尼于德黑兰一家医院去世不到一天后，伊朗已经任命了他的继任者。

sentences.en: 49-year-old Ali Khamenei was today chosen Khomeini's religious successor by Iran's Council of Senior Clerics.
sentences.zh: 49岁的阿里·哈梅内伊今天被伊朗高级神职人员委员会选为霍梅尼的宗教继任者。

sentences.en: It is widely expected that...
sentences.zh: 人们普遍预计……

sentences.en: Mr. Khamenei succeeded him in 1989.
sentences.zh: 哈梅内伊先生于1989年继任。

sentences.en: Ayatollah Khomeini unleashed anti-Western passions throughout the Islamic world.
sentences.zh: 阿亚图拉·霍梅尼在整个伊斯兰世界引发了反西方情绪。

sentences.en: Today, there were thinly veiled hopes that his successors would be less effective, if not more friendly.
sentences.zh: 今天，人们隐约希望他的继任者能不那么有效，甚至更友好一些。

sentences.en: And it is said that while the first supreme leader led a revolution, Mr. Khamenei led a state.
sentences.zh: 人们常说，第一任最高领袖领导了一场革命，而哈梅内伊先生领导了一个国家。

sentences.en: He really is the ruler who made sure that the Islamic Republic went from a revolutionary idea into a state that entrenched power.
sentences.zh: 他确实是一位确保伊斯兰共和国从一个革命理念转变为一个巩固权力的国家的统治者。

sentences.en: The Islamic Republic of Iran that we know today, that has influence over proxy militant groups and, you know, has a nuclear power and missile and military power,
sentences.zh: 我们今天所知的伊朗伊斯兰共和国，对代理人武装组织有影响力，拥有核力量、导弹和军事力量，

sentences.en: was all the vision of Mr. Khamenei.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是哈梅内伊先生的愿景。

sentences.en: Not only was he the religious leader of Shias around the world, but his Iran would also be this country that led anti-imperialism, anti-Americanism.
sentences.zh: 他不仅是世界各地什叶派的宗教领袖，他的伊朗也成为了领导反帝国主义、反美主义的国家。

sentences.en: Anti-Israelism.
sentences.zh: 反以色列主义。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In one of his notorious quotes, he said,
sentences.zh: 在他最臭名昭著的言论之一中，他说：

sentences.en: The reason Hamas now has rockets and can attack Israel is because of us.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯现在之所以有火箭弹并能攻击以色列，是因为我们。

sentences.en: We enabled them to go from rocks and arrows to missiles and guns with our training and with our funding.
sentences.zh: 我们通过培训和资助，使他们能够从使用石头和弓箭转变为使用导弹和枪支。

sentences.en: And of course, the thing that he is known for is his role in domestic repression.
sentences.zh: 当然，他最出名的是他在国内镇压中的角色。

sentences.en: For a few days, it looked like the start of a second revolution.
sentences.zh: 有几天，这看起来像是第二次革命的开始。

sentences.en: Students on the campus of Tehran University demanding political and social reform.
sentences.zh: 德黑兰大学校园里的学生要求政治和社会改革。

sentences.en: But the response was swift and violent.
sentences.zh: 但回应是迅速而暴力的。

sentences.en: Mr. Khamenei had absolute power.
sentences.zh: 哈梅内伊先生拥有绝对权力。

sentences.en: He is known for never giving an inch to calls for reform.
sentences.zh: 他以从不向改革呼声妥协而闻名。

sentences.en: Sent in to crush this youthful idealism.
sentences.zh: 派人去粉碎这种年轻人的理想主义。

sentences.en: Not the police or army, but a militia called the Besiege.
sentences.zh: 不是警察或军队，而是一支名为“巴斯基”的民兵组织。

sentences.en: Defenders of the fundamentalist revolution.
sentences.zh: 原教旨主义革命的捍卫者。

sentences.en: Sidelining political opponents.
sentences.zh: 排挤政治对手。

sentences.en: This government won't allow us to say what we want.
sentences.zh: 这个政府不允许我们说出我们想说的话。

sentences.en: Jailing dissidents.
sentences.zh: 监禁异见人士。

sentences.en: The government's response has been violence.
sentences.zh: 政府的回应是暴力。

sentences.en: Armor-clad police attacking protesters from the backs of speeding motorcycles.
sentences.zh: 身穿盔甲的警察从飞驰的摩托车后座上攻击抗议者。

sentences.en: Calling for brutal and lethal crackdowns on protesters.
sentences.zh: 呼吁对抗议者进行残酷和致命的镇压。

sentences.en: These are some of the most recent images coming out of Iran.
sentences.zh: 这些是伊朗最近传出的一些画面。

sentences.en: The regime cut off the internet in Iran on the 8th of January, hoping to prevent coverage of its crackdown on protesters.
sentences.zh: 该政权于1月8日切断了伊朗的互联网，希望阻止对其镇压抗议者的报道。

sentences.en: Including the recent wave in January where he personally ordered the shoot-to-kill order.

sentences.en: He's also one of the names that I have heard.
sentences.zh: 因为这些人中的每一个都是体制的一部分，并在47年来作为该政府一部分的压迫、杀戮和镇压中扮演了角色。

sentences.en: I've also heard the name of former President Hassan Rouhani, who's kind of a moderate cleric, but he's sort of been outcast from the close circle of Mr. Khamenei.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，美国和特朗普总统最终是否会决定，他不希望冒伊朗不稳定的风险，不希望冒内战的风险，

sentences.en: So these are some of the names I've heard.
sentences.zh: 而宁愿与体制内愿意做出让步或不做出让步的人接触。

sentences.en: But I want to mention here that for that 80 percent who want wholesome change and for the opposition and dissidents,
sentences.zh: 我们今天听到特朗普总统说，他愿意与伊朗的新领导人对话，并且他听说有一些继任选择。

sentences.en: no figure that is associated with the Islamic Republic's regime is going to be acceptable.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他是在向伊朗政权发出信号，如果你确实有一个愿意给我想要的东西，并在核、军事、导弹和政策上做出我想要的让步的人物——

sentences.en: Because every single one of these people was part of a system and had a role in those oppressions and killings and repressions that have been part and parcel of this government for 47 years.
sentences.zh: 那么我会支持那位领导人。

sentences.en: But the question is whether the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果不支持他，至少我会接触并考虑那位领导人的可能性。

sentences.en: and President Trump will ultimately decide that he doesn't want to risk instability in Iran, he doesn't want to risk civil war,
sentences.zh: 这对伊朗人民对民主和自由的渴望是有害的，但政治是不可预测的。

sentences.en: and would rather engage with someone from that system that would be willing to make concessions or not.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we heard President Trump say today that he's open to speaking to Iran's new leaders and that he's heard that there are some options for succession.
sentences.zh: 从非常现实的意义上讲，这与政权更迭背道而驰，所以特朗普总统将不得不决定什么对他来说才是最重要的。

sentences.en: So I think he's kind of signaling to the Iranian regime that if you do have a character who is willing to give me what I want and make the kind of concessions that I want on nuclear and military and missiles and policies—
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Then I will back that leader.
sentences.zh: 改变政权还是建立一个稳定的伊朗，这两者可能会发生冲突。

sentences.en: If not back him, at least I'll engage and entertain the possibility of that leader.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That will be detrimental to the aspirations of democracy and freedom for the Iranian people, but politics are unpredictable.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我认为这对伊朗国内外的许多人来说将是巨大的失望，因为，你知道，特朗普总统，出于我们谈到的所有原因，

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 关于那80%庆祝伊朗事件和战争的人，他被视为一个目前帮助了他们实现变革愿望的人物。

sentences.en: In a very real sense, that would be at odds with regime change, and so President Trump is going to have to decide what really matters most to him.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这种情况可能会迅速改变，如果美国与哈梅内伊先生的继任者达成协议，他们可能会感到被背叛。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，无论接下来谁领导伊朗，我都在想，过去几天的事件是否多多少少保证了它的政府真的再也不会和以前一样了，

sentences.en: Changing the regime or creating a stable Iran, those may be in conflict.
sentences.zh: 即使是政权内部的人在管理它，我真正的意思是，很难想象伊朗会回到代理人和国家支持的恐怖主义体系，

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 那正是哈梅内伊35年统治的定义，原因很简单，随着时间的推移，这导致了他自己的死亡。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think it would be hugely disappointing to many people in Iran, both inside and outside, because, you know, President Trump, for all the reasons we talked about,
sentences.zh: 这让美国和以色列相信，解决问题的唯一办法就是除掉领导人。

sentences.en: about sort of the 80 percent that are celebrating the events in Iran and the war, he's seen as a figure who has helped their aspirations for change right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们所知道的伊斯兰共和国已经结束了。

sentences.en: But I think that that could quickly change, and they may feel betrayed if the U.S.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: strikes a deal with the successors of Mr. Khamenei.
sentences.zh: 我认为哈梅内伊经营的国家，那个敌视美国、敌视阿拉伯邻国、敌视以色列，

sentences.en: Well, no matter who leads Iran next, I wonder if the events of the past few days more or less guarantees that its government is really never the same,
sentences.zh: 并定义了武装、恐怖、劫持人质和镇压本国公民的国家，是不可持续的。

sentences.en: even if it's an insider from the regime running it, and by that I really mean it's hard to fathom Iran returning to the system of proxies and state-sponsored terror
sentences.zh: 它是不可持续的，无法在中东的新现实中生存，在那里我们看到以色列在10月7日之后将安全和生存置于一切之上。

sentences.en: that really defined Khamenei's 35 years in power for the simple reason that, over time, it resulted in his own death.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是一个会被其不安分的人口所容忍的伊朗，除非它发生改变。

sentences.en: It made the U.S.
sentences.zh: 考虑到我们在该地区和针对阿拉伯国家看到的所有袭击，我不认为伊朗的邻国会容忍那样的国家，

sentences.en: and it made Israel believe that the only way to solve the problem was to take out the leader.
sentences.zh: 以及那种他们面临被攻击风险的感觉，还有隔壁那个没人知道它会做什么、如何反应的不可预测的政府。

sentences.en: I think the Islamic Republic, as we knew it, is over.
sentences.zh: 而且我不认为美国也一定会容忍它。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I think the state that Mr. Khamenei ran, which was hostile to the U.S., hostile to its Arab neighbors, hostile to Israel,
sentences.zh: 我认为哈梅内伊先生所治理的国家，那个敌视美国、敌视阿拉伯邻国、敌视以色列的国家，

sentences.en: and defined militancy and terror and hostage-taking and repression of its own citizens, is not sustainable.
sentences.zh: 那个将激进主义、恐怖主义、劫持人质以及镇压本国公民定义为常态的国家，是无法持续下去的。

sentences.en: It's not sustainable and cannot survive in the new realities of the Middle East, where we've seen Israel sort of prioritize its safety and survival above all else post-October 7.
sentences.zh: 它是不可持续的，无法在中东的新现实中生存下去，因为我们已经看到以色列在10月7日之后，将自身的安全与生存置于一切之上。

sentences.en: I don't think it is an Iran that will be tolerated by its restive population that won't change.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这样一个伊朗能被其躁动不安且渴望变革的人民所容忍。

sentences.en: And given all the attacks we've seen in the region and against Arab states, I don't think Iran's neighbors will tolerate that kind of a state
sentences.zh: 鉴于我们在该地区以及针对阿拉伯国家所看到的所有袭击，我认为伊朗的邻国不会再容忍这样一个国家，

sentences.en: and this feeling that they're at risk of being attacked and sort of an unpredictable government next door that nobody knows, you know, what it will do and how it will react.
sentences.zh: 也不会再容忍那种时刻面临被攻击风险的感觉，以及隔壁那个没人知道它会做什么、会如何反应的不可预测的政府。

sentences.en: And I don't think the United States will necessarily tolerate it either.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为美国也不一定会容忍它。

sentences.en: So I think all the odds are stacked against the Islamic Republic continuing as it has been for the past 47 years.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，伊斯兰共和国要像过去47年那样继续存在下去，几乎是不可能的了。

sentences.en: Well, just to end, Farnaz, I wonder, to that point, what members of the Iranian opposition and the expat world diaspora, you even,
sentences.zh: 法娜兹，最后我想问一下，就这一点而言，伊朗反对派成员和海外侨民，甚至包括你，

sentences.en: what you're allowing yourself to hope for and to dream of for Iran in this moment of such extraordinary flux and fear, but also possibility.
sentences.zh: 在这个充满巨大变动、恐惧，但也充满可能性的时刻，你允许自己对伊朗抱有什么样的希望和梦想？

sentences.en: Um, I'm Iranian-American, and on Friday, I thought that the possibility of ever visiting Iran,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是美籍伊朗人。周五那天，我以为自己还能去伊朗，

sentences.en: of visiting my father's gravesite, or seeing my elderly relatives, was a distant dream.
sentences.zh: 去祭拜我父亲的墓地，或者探望年迈亲人的可能性，已经是一个遥不可及的梦想了。

sentences.en: Today, I have hope.
sentences.zh: 今天，我有了希望。

sentences.en: Of returning.
sentences.zh: 重返故土的希望。

sentences.en: Of returning.
sentences.zh: 重返故土的希望。

sentences.en: A pretty modest goal.
sentences.zh: 一个相当卑微的目标。

sentences.en: You know, that's what a lot of Iranians who've been exiled and who can't go back say.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多流亡在外、无法回国的伊朗人都是这么说的。

sentences.en: They say that it's pretty bare minimum to want to see your relatives and visit your home country, and it's a right that has been robbed from many people.
sentences.zh: 他们说，想见见亲人、回祖国看看，这已经是最低限度的要求了，而这却是许多人被剥夺的权利。

sentences.en: And I think many Iranians the world over have a glimmer of hope.
sentences.zh: 我认为全世界许多伊朗人都看到了一丝希望的曙光。

sentences.en: Well, let me ask about a perhaps less modest set of possibilities.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我来问问一套可能不那么“卑微”的可能性吧。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about the people who were taking shots on Saturday.
sentences.zh: 我在想那些周六走上街头的人们。

sentences.en: I mean, what do they dare to think about beyond just visiting relatives back in Iran?
sentences.zh: 我是说，除了回伊朗探亲，他们还敢于去想些什么？

sentences.en: They dare to dream of a free Iran, where political prisoners are free, where young people who take to the streets to demand for a better living are not shot and killed,
sentences.zh: 他们敢于梦想一个自由的伊朗，那里政治犯能重获自由，年轻人走上街头争取更好的生活时不会被枪杀，

sentences.en: and people are not struggling to make ends meet because it's a resource-rich country, where parents are not mourning their children.
sentences.zh: 人们不必为生计发愁，因为那是一个资源丰富的国家，父母不必为失去孩子而哀悼。

sentences.en: Watching the videos of people taking to the streets and chanting, freedom, freedom, in reaction to Mr. Khamenei's killing,
sentences.zh: 看着人们走上街头，高呼“自由，自由”，以回应哈梅内伊先生的杀戮行为的视频，

sentences.en: it may sound to an American or Western audience that this is a modest aspiration, but I think for the Iranian people who have sort of long aspired
sentences.zh: 对于美国或西方观众来说，这听起来可能是一个卑微的愿望，但我认为对于那些长期以来一直渴望

sentences.en: and work toward having a free, democratic, secular country,
sentences.zh: 并致力于建立一个自由、民主、世俗国家的伊朗人民来说，

sentences.en: this is a big dream.
sentences.zh: 这是一个伟大的梦想。

sentences.en: And as a reporter who's covered Iran for three decades,
sentences.zh: 作为一名报道伊朗三十年的记者，

sentences.en: I never thought that I would be writing this news or, you know, reporting this.
sentences.zh: 我从未想过自己会写出这样的新闻，或者说，报道这些事情。

sentences.en: So I looked at the front page of the New York Times today with the headline and thought, wow, this is a headline and a story I never thought I would write in my lifetime yet.
sentences.zh: 所以我今天看着《纽约时报》的头版标题时心想，哇，这真是我有生之年从未想过会写出的标题和故事。

sentences.en: Well, Farnaz, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，法娜兹，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，迈克尔。

sentences.en: In an interview on Sunday night with The Times,
sentences.zh: 在周日晚间接受《时报》采访时，

sentences.en: President Trump said that the American military assault against Iran could last up to four to five weeks.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统表示，美国对伊朗的军事打击可能会持续四到五周。

sentences.en: When pressed on his plan for who should lead Iran's government, the president offered several seemingly inconsistent visions.
sentences.zh: 当被追问他关于谁应该领导伊朗政府的计划时，总统提出了几种看似不一致的设想。

sentences.en: One scenario, he said, was that the United States identified a cooperative leader from inside the regime.
sentences.zh: 他说，一种方案是美国从伊朗政权内部确定一位愿意合作的领导人。

sentences.en: Another scenario, he said, was that Iran's elite military forces would simply lay down their weapons and surrender to the people of Iran.
sentences.zh: 他说，另一种方案是伊朗的精锐部队直接放下武器，向伊朗人民投降。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: The Constitution can't be changed by statute.
sentences.zh: 宪法不能通过法规来修改。

sentences.en: The Constitution says no declaration of war without Congress.
sentences.zh: 宪法规定，未经国会批准不得宣战。

sentences.en: The president has called this war against Iran.
sentences.zh: 总统称这次行动为对伊朗的战争。

sentences.en: On Sunday, congressional Democrats questioned the legality of President Trump's military strikes against Iran, saying that it was a clear-cut case where he needed Congress's
sentences.zh: 周日，国会民主党人质疑特朗普总统对伊朗进行军事打击的合法性，称这是一个明显的案例，他需要国会的

sentences.en: approval but failed to seek it.
sentences.zh: 批准却未寻求批准。

sentences.en: One of those Democrats, Senator Tim Kaine of Virginia, has introduced a resolution seeking to end the use of American military forces in Iran.
sentences.zh: 其中一位民主党人，弗吉尼亚州参议员蒂姆·凯恩，提出了一项决议，寻求终止美国在伊朗使用军事力量。

sentences.en: The president not only did not come to Congress to seek a debate or vote, he acted without even notification to the vast majority of us.
sentences.zh: 总统不仅没有来国会寻求辩论或投票，甚至在行动前都没有通知我们绝大多数人。

sentences.en: This is an illegal war.
sentences.zh: 这是一场非法的战争。

sentences.en: And as markets opened on Sunday night, oil prices rose 10 percent, highlighting the economic risks of the conflict in Iran.
sentences.zh: 随着周日晚间市场开盘，油价上涨了10%，凸显了伊朗冲突带来的经济风险。

sentences.en: The U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran could severely restrict oil and gas supplies around the world.
sentences.zh: 美以对伊朗的袭击可能会严重限制全球的石油和天然气供应。

sentences.en: Even if the disruption is brief, it will almost certainly make energy more expensive around the world.
sentences.zh: 即使中断时间很短，也几乎肯定会让全球能源价格变得更加昂贵。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Jessica Chung, Mary Wilson, and Claire Tennesketter.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由杰西卡·钟、玛丽·威尔逊和克莱尔·坦内斯凯特制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Liz O'Balen and Paige Cowett.
sentences.zh: 由利兹·奥巴伦和佩奇·考特编辑。

sentences.en: Contains music by Alisha B'Etoot and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 包含艾丽莎·贝图特和丹·鲍威尔的音乐。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly创作。

sentences.en: The episode was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由克里斯·伍德担任工程制作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为您准备节日期间的待客之道。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是睡到不省人事。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 您可以在《纽约时报》应用程序或您喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《Wirecutter秀》。
